_note: Illustrative excerpt only: 3 of the ~7 topics a real decomposition of `dictionaries` would have. Shows the expected depth, linking and tone. Prerequisite IDs are examples of earlier-wave topics.

dictionaries.notes: Remaining topics in a full decomposition: iterate keys/values/items, get() and default values, membership and KeyError, grouping values into lists.

topics.title: Creating a dictionary and looking up values
topics.summary: Write a dict literal mapping keys to values and read a value by key, including what happens with a missing key.

knowledge_points.title: Dict literal and lookup by key
knowledge_points.practice: Predict the printed value for a 3-entry dict; write the lookup expression for a named key.

knowledge_points.title: Why a dict beats a list of pairs
knowledge_points.worked_example: Finding 'bo' in [('ana', 31), ('bo', 27)] needs a loop; ages['bo'] does not. Same data, one-step lookup.
knowledge_points.practice: Choose the structure that answers a lookup question in one expression; convert a short list of pairs to a dict literal.

knowledge_points.title: Missing keys raise KeyError
knowledge_points.worked_example: ages['cy'] raises KeyError: 'cy'. Keys are case-sensitive: ages['Ana'] also fails.
knowledge_points.practice: Predict whether each lookup prints a value or raises KeyError.

topics.title: Adding, updating and deleting entries
topics.summary: Mutate a dict: assign to a new key, overwrite an existing key, delete with del and pop.

knowledge_points.title: Assigning to a new key adds it
knowledge_points.practice: Predict the dict after a sequence of assignments.

knowledge_points.title: Assigning to an existing key overwrites it
knowledge_points.worked_example:
stock['apple'] = stock['apple'] + 1  # 4
The old value is read, then replaced; keys stay unique.
knowledge_points.practice: Predict values after mixed add/overwrite steps; fill in the line that increments a count.

knowledge_points.title: Removing entries with del and pop
knowledge_points.worked_example:
del stock['pear']
n = stock.pop('apple')  # n == 4, key removed
pop returns the value; both raise KeyError if absent.
knowledge_points.practice: Predict the dict and returned value; spot the line that raises KeyError.

topics.title: Counting occurrences with a dictionary
topics.summary: The histogram idiom: loop over items and increment a per-key count, first with an if/else, then with get(key, 0).

knowledge_points.title: Count with if/else
knowledge_points.practice: Reorder the lines of the counting loop; predict counts for a 5-word list.

knowledge_points.title: Count with get(key, 0)
knowledge_points.practice: Rewrite an if/else counter using get; predict get() results for present and missing keys.

knowledge_points.title: Count characters, then find the most common
knowledge_points.practice: Write a function returning the most frequent character; fix a version that resets the count inside the loop.
